newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl admits could do more to reform Germany.
newsitem.headline: Kohl admits could do more to reform Germany.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday welcomed scolding comments by President Roman Herzog about a deadlock in tax, pension and labour reforms in Bonn and admitted that changes were needed.
"This country needs a jolt and we must change," Kohl told a meeting of regional leaders of his Christian Democrat party (CDU), echoing a hard-hitting speech Herzog made on Saturday.

"We have all made mistakes in the last few years, myself included," he said. "Much has happened in Germany in these 15 years (since I became chancellor)... The President is right that we could do more."
Kohl said despite varying interests all parties had to serve their country and overcome the challenges facing the country on the threshold of the 21st century.
Herzog, whose largely ceremonial office is above partisan wrangling, scolded the whole political class and said Germany could not afford further delays in reform.

Kohl's admission that the government could do more contrasted with the response of other politicians who welcomed Herzog's comments but sought to shift the blame for delays in key reforms onto others.

His top deputy Wolfgang Schaeuble said on Monday the widespread public impression of a political logjam in Bonn was wrong even though tax reform talks between the governent and the Social Democrat (SPD) opposition collapsed last week.

Schaeuble said the centre-right government had made important breakthroughs with its efforts to stimulate job creation since embarking on a reform drive at the beginning of last year and blamed the SPD for the breakdown in tax talks.
But Kohl said it was the role of the head of state to point out what he saw from his point of view.
